prompt.context: PayCo is a credit card company with over $5B in revenues in 2010. Their recently developed Tap & Go proprietary technology has been very successful, and they now want to leverage it to the cash-dominated public transportation sector. PayCo has asked for our help in commercializing Tap & Go for transit transactions.
prompt.question: PayCo wants to enter the public transportation payments market using its Tap & Go technology. Given a 5-year investment horizon (2011-2015), advise PayCo on whether and how to enter this market.

clarifying_info.a: Tap & Go is a feature that allows consumers to pay by simply tapping their credit card or mobile phone on a payment reader at checkout. It is currently used for small purchases (under $25) at places like supermarkets, fast-food outlets, bars, and parking lots.
Our client has a 5-year investment horizon from 2011 to 2015.
There are two major competitors in the market, including PayCo. They both offer Tap & Go services.

clarifying_info.q: What is the main payment method for public transportation currently?
clarifying_info.a: Assume that the main payment method for public transportation is cash.
Commuters, the majority of whom have credit cards.
PayCo has a strong track record with Tap & Go and a good brand name. Since public transportation is currently cash dominated, it does not have strong relationships with transit providers.

exhibits.title: City and Transportation Market Data
exhibits.shows: A table comparing three cities (New York, London, Tokyo) across city-level metrics and two modes of transportation (Subway and Bus), including ridership, annual revenues, expected year of implementation, and probability of implementation.

exhibits.title: Economics of the New York Subway Tap & Go Market
exhibits.shows: A table showing annual transaction volumes and marketing/SG&A costs for the New York Subway Tap & Go market from 2011 to 2015, along with the license fee, transaction fee rate, and transaction cost rate.

framework: Market: Market size and growth potential of Tap & Go for transit; current competitors and new entrants offering similar technology; substitutes such as Google Wallet or other mobile payment methods

Company: Capabilities including patent protection, expertise with Tap & Go, and partnerships that can be leveraged; Execution including access to transportation authorities, regulatory barriers, capital available, and opportunity cost
Customers: Commuter segmentation, average spend on public transportation, willingness to adopt new payment technologies
Economics: Revenue = (license fee + per-transaction fee) x volume; Costs = fixed (R&D, SG&A, advertising, IT, support) + variable (cost per transaction) + upfront investment

questions.prompt: Question 1: PayCo has identified three key cities on which it would like to focus. As a first step, it would like to enter one city and service one mode of transportation. Based on the information in Exhibit 1, and given a 5-year horizon (2011-2015), which city and mode of transportation should PayCo target?
questions.guidance: The interviewee should focus on the most relevant data. Not all data points are necessary. Since fee rates, costs, and penetration rates are unknown and assumed equal across cities, the candidate should use an Expected Value approach: EV = Annual Revenue x Number of Years Active x Probability of Implementation. The city and mode with the highest EV is the best target. Population growth and GDP can be used as qualitative support.

math.setup: EV = Annual Revenue x Years Active x Probability of Implementation. Years active = 2015 minus expected year of implementation + 1. Assume discount rate = 0%.
steps: NYC Subway: $12B x 4 years (2012-2015) x 90% = $43.2B x fee%
NYC Bus: $5.4B x 4 years (2012-2015) x 80% = $17.3B x fee%
London Subway: $13B x 4 years (2012-2015) x 70% = $36.4B x fee%
London Bus: $9B x 2 years (2014-2015) x 90% = $16.2B x fee%
Tokyo Subway: $16B x 2 years (2014-2015) x 20% = $6.4B x fee% (note: casebook states $9.6B, implying 3 years or rounding)
Tokyo Bus: $11.5B x 3 years (2013-2015) x 40% = $13.8B x fee%
math.answer: NYC Subway has the highest expected value at approximately $43.2B x fee%. New York also has strong population growth (0.9%) and the highest GDP among the three cities at $1,406B, further supporting market entry.

questions.prompt: Question 2: Our analysis of the New York subway market yielded the following results (Exhibit 2). Would PayCo be able to break even within 5 years? The upfront investment for the launch is $5M.
questions.guidance: The candidate must calculate annual profit each year using the exhibit data, then accumulate profits to determine when cumulative profit covers the $5M upfront investment. Key calculations: (1) transaction fee revenue = 0.2% x annual transactions; (2) cost per transaction = $0.004 x (annual transactions / $2.5 average size). Annual profit = license fee + transaction fee revenue - transaction cost - A&P - SG&A.

math.setup: Annual Profit = (License Fee + Transaction Fee Revenue) - (Transaction Cost + A&P + SG&A). Upfront investment = $5M. Breakeven when cumulative profit >= $5M.
math.answer: PayCo breaks even in 2014. Cumulative profits reach $6.3M by end of 2014, covering the $5M upfront investment within the 5-year horizon.

recommendation: PayCo should enter the New York Subway market: it has the highest revenue potential ($43.2B x fee%), a high probability of implementation (90%), and a break-even period shorter than the 5-year horizon (achieved in 2014).
It would make sense to enter additional cities and modes of transportation within the next 5 years, leveraging the New York experience.
risks: Our projections of the implementation probability and number of transactions may be inflated.
Response from our major competitor could erode market share or trigger a price war.
Regulations resulting from privacy and security concerns could delay or block implementation.
next_steps: Create an implementation plan for entering the New York Subway market.
Build relationships with the Metropolitan Transportation Authority (MTA).
Analyze additional markets to identify further expansion opportunities.
